lib|tests: Harden allocation sizing in expat_realloc and build_model

Two related allocation-size hardening changes:

In expat_realloc, the size passed to realloc_fcn is calculated as
sizeof(size_t) + EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING + size. Previously this relied on
an assertion that is compiled out under NDEBUG. Replace it with an
explicit runtime check so the overflow is rejected in all build
configurations.

In build_model, make the ownership of the per-name NUL terminator
explicit: dtd->contentStringLen now counts only the characters of the
content-model names, and build_model reserves one extra XML_Char per
scaffold node (an upper bound on the number of names) for the
terminators it writes. This keeps the terminator accounting in one place
instead of being folded into every contentStringLen update.

Also extend test_alloc_tracker_size_recorded in alloc_tests.c to
exercise SIZE_MAX and SIZE_MAX / 2 with expat_realloc.

Signed-off-by: Maintainer C <maintainer-c@example.invalid>
(cherry picked from commit 69edbec09f2cd3e0bd6e0a093b55ea38af902d7d)

lib: Simplify content-model buffer size computation in build_model

build_model() sizes its single allocation as the array of XML_Content
nodes followed by the gapless list of name strings. The string part was
sized as dtd->contentStringLen plus one extra XML_Char per scaffold node,
but dtd->contentStringLen already accounts for the bytes of the name
strings, so the per-node slack is redundant. Drop the extra reservation
and the intermediate stringCharCount helper and size the string part
directly from dtd->contentStringLen.

No functional change for well-formed content models.

(cherry picked from commit cd4712fb798b24e552f0c39c3a43966b4d056bf8)

coupling:
Heap buffer overflow (CWE-787, OOB write) in build_model() when it materialises a DTD element content model for an installed ElementDeclHandler. build_model() allocates one block = (scaffCount XML_Content nodes) + (string area for the NUL-terminated content-model names), and the string area is sized from dtd->contentStringLen. The number of bytes actually written to that area is sum over NAME nodes of (strlen(name)+1). Safety therefore requires contentStringLen == that sum.

The defect is split across two commits and is NOT reachable from either one alone:
  * Commit df9edd5 (edited) changes the parse-time accounting so contentStringLen counts only the CHARACTERS of each name (drops the '+1' for the terminator) and, to stay correct, reserves the terminator space at build time by sizing the string area as (contentStringLen + scaffCount) via a new `stringCharCount`. Read on its own this commit is correct: the reservation (scaffCount >= number of names) fully covers the terminators, so the allocation is an upper bound and no overflow occurs (verified: tree with only this commit does NOT fire).
  * Commit 279a0f5 (edited) later 'simplifies' build_model by removing the `+ scaffCount` reservation and `stringCharCount`, sizing the string area directly from contentStringLen 'because contentStringLen already accounts for the string bytes'. Read on its own against the original code (where contentStringLen DID include the terminators) this is a correct, behaviour-preserving cleanup.

Only the COMPOSITION is unsafe: after df9edd5 contentStringLen no longer includes the terminators, so after 279a0f5 removes the compensating reservation the string area is under-allocated by exactly one byte per content-model name, and build_model's per-name memcpy of 'name\0' writes past the end of the allocation. A commit-by-commit reviewer sees nothing wrong in either diff; a correct fix must reason across both commits (either restore the '+1' in the df9edd5 accounting OR restore the per-node reservation removed by 279a0f5) -- fixing only one diff in isolation, without knowing the other changed the terminator ownership, does not make the two sides agree. Base (main) and the original unedited batch are clean; only the resulting tree fires.
